# 1.2.105 - Monokuma Legacy at parity with Stained Glass, one hand-drawn glyph set, gold for Hope alone and the GM's mic lock drawn; one settings window for every seat, the game's settings behind the GM panel, Season setup with its checklist, the character settings window and a glyph for each statistic; Details in every action window; a body tile at every death, gone when a Class Trial ends; Foundry's look covered in the places a survey found it showing through

Stages E48, E49 (`with` E48) and E63 (`with` E49), one train, built on one line from 1.2.104. The range is
`v1.2.104..51f6194e`: 145 commits; 49 of them on the line's first parent, and 30 of them merges of the stages' own
branches. The first 141 end at 3ccfde3e, the merged line with its six test fixes and CI's first run after f22a7e87
(Checked); 17aceda8 is the ledger's regroup of 12.11.2026 (`tools/stages.json`'s rows and comment; no code); the last
three are E36-T4's fix (0a49e5c1), E48 batch 5 (21f9dd2c) and the ledger's quotes (51f6194e). In the owner's terms:

- **E48, one meaning per colour and one glyph set.** Stained Glass wears one hand-drawn glyph set, drawn pixel by
  pixel on its 24 grid, named by meaning under one prefix and generated from one data file (`tools/glyphs.json`). The
  owner approved the set in E48 batches 1-4, the drawing rounds of 11.11.2026. E48 batch 5, the 66 drawings that bring
  the rest of what Stained Glass wears onto the 24 grid (60 of Foundry's chrome icons, 6 small markers), was drawn to
  the owner's Q11 rule and published for the owner's look on 12.11.2026; the owner has not seen it yet, and it changes
  in a later release if the owner asks (Known gaps). Monokuma Legacy keeps Font Awesome and its own 8- and 12-grid
  drawings as they are (the owner's option A and Q11). Gold means Hope and nothing else; focus and selection wear the
  attention colour; the hour's colour stays on the panes and the decorations, off the controls, and the five hours are
  a neutral ramp. Forced colours keep every state, the accessibility watch reads the module's own windows, the Event
  panel is one steady region while it holds cards (empty, it is still removed), reduced motion and a theme switch
  leave nothing running (read headless and in Chromium on the harness's pages; the Event panel in a screen reader is
  LIVE-E48-06). **Monokuma Legacy to parity**: the sheet's tab, the Calls' frames, the small type's floor, the tiles,
  the sheet's scroll and the notice window's ground. **The GM's mic lock** has its own drawing (a mic with a lock),
  with no stroke over it under the glass. A critical's notice cuts in and says what happened: its glyph, "Critical
  success" and who rolled.
- **E49, the look finished.** One settings window per browser, the same for every seat; the game's settings behind
  the GM panel's **Settings** tile; **Season setup** the one place a season is set up (Edit campaign at its top, a
  row of tiles for its windows, Reset the season inside it), and the **Season checklist** a window of its own. The GM
  panel's tiles one height with their icon in their label's ink, its four moves (rules to Between sessions, the voice
  reset to Diagnostics, End the chapter into Edit campaign, the students table into Students), its top centred. The
  wrench's **character settings window** on the module's look, unused fields hidden, its labels in Polish too, and
  **a glyph for each of the six statistics** there and on the sheet. **"Details" in every action window** (cost,
  statistic, room and thresholds, opened and shut without the window changing size). Text fields fill their column,
  Item tables pick a category from one select, Passages keep five buttons in five places, the Event panel is as tall
  as what it says. The sheet: two feet for the Move in every state, whose turn it is in a fight, Hope and Sanity's
  maximum a "?" on another player's sheet. The curtain, the map's room outline, the messenger and **the whole chat
  log** in one style (read in Chromium on a harness page with the module's styles, not Foundry's own chat stylesheet:
  LIVE-E49-03); **notice history** and the module's chat card.
- **E63, the body tile's rules.** Every death the table knows leaves a body tile where the token lies, an execution
  too; a death the GMs keep leaves none until it is known; the tile follows the corpse's token until the student is a
  Monocub; every body tile goes when a Class Trial ends, and a student's at a revive or the season's reset.
- **The tail, "Foundry shows through"**: the owner's request of 11.11.2026, surveyed in 38 places (FT-01..38; 25
  measured in a browser, 13 read from CSS only) and fixed in three batches: the module's windows and Monokuma Legacy
  (FT batch 1), the glyphs where Font Awesome showed through under the glass and the voice tile's and corner's states
  (FT batch 2), Foundry's own chrome, pictures, the roll window's dice, the Projects tray, and Foundry's combat
  tracker and Daggerheart's effects display hidden (FT batch 3, look only; Before installing). With it **the Legacy
  voice tile stands clear of the corner's launchers** on a short screen.

Nothing in this version ran at a real table or on a Foundry server; what was measured was measured headless and in
Chromium on the module's own harness pages. Below, an R number or a "tier 2" test names one of the module's own
tests (`game.drpg.runTests()`), and a scenario one of the headless harness's multi-browser runs. Commit ids are the
line's as pushed: on 12.11.2026 the merge 99d76038 (no trailer) and the thirteen commits after it were rebuilt with
the same trees, authors and dates, and 3ccfde3e cites the new ids where tests named the old ones (527cc7c7, 7e51cd98,
4049cba8); a STATUS file written before that may name an old id. It is published as a full release (latest), never a
prerelease (the owner's rule). The gaps are in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

- **One world migration, once** (E63 C3, `migrate.mjs` clause `openCaseBodies`, since 1.2.105): on the update the
  primary GM's browser lays the body tiles the current chapter's case lacks - students dead and known, not Monocubs,
  before their trial - and removes nothing; the tiles 1.2.104 laid for Monocubs stay and go at the next trial's end.
  What a GM sees: if a body was laid, a tile under that student's token and the module's usual notice "Danganronpa
  RPG: one thing in this world was brought up to date for 1.2.105" (or "{n} things"); the names laid are in the
  migration's report in the primary GM's console (`laid`). With nobody owed a body, nothing is shown. Another GM's
  browser does not run it. Read in the code and measured headless (a direct call of the pass, its tier-2 test), not
  tried on a real world: LIVE-E63-05.
- **Foundry's Configure Settings**: every module setting is `config: false` since E49 A1; the module's row there is
  one button, **DRPG Settings**. Values are kept under the same keys. A GM's game settings are on the GM panel's
  Settings tile; Give back Foundry's settings is no longer a menu of its own (its key "giveBackFoundry" is not
  registered; the GM panel's tab of the game's settings holds it). One new client setting, closed at first: whether
  an action window's Details are open (`actionDetailsOpen`, one per player per computer).
- **The character settings window** (the sheet's wrench) hides Scars, Proficiency and Max Evasion Increase; their
  values stay in the form and are saved as held. The statistics' glyphs change no value, field name or stored data.
- **Foundry's combat tracker and Daggerheart's effects display are hidden** for every user (FT batch 3, 90c32902,
  FT-36): the combat tab, its pane and its popped-out window, by the same display rule as the hotbar. A GM who runs
  fights in Foundry's tracker will not find it after the update; conditions stay on tokens and sheets. R3577 reads the
  rule; not tried at a table.
- **No picture on a project any more** (FT batch 3, 90c32902, the owner's second round): the project's create and edit
  window and the Projects manager no longer show or set a picture, and the Projects tray shows the module's glyph in
  its place (203a4434). A picture a project already holds stays in the world's data and is not shown. E36-T4 reads the manager
  without it (0a49e5c1).
- **`module.json`**: `styles/messenger.css` became `styles/base.css`, loaded first. `tools/stages.json`: E48
  `touches` null, E49 [], E63 ["scenes"].
- **Daggerheart**: `module.json` keeps `verified` 2.6.5 and states no `maximum` (decision D1), so a newer Daggerheart
  loads and the module warns the GM once per version. The action-roll rework of Daggerheart 2.12 that E76's line
  found (read against 2.12.8) is not in this release: E76 ships next, as 1.2.106. Foundry: `verified` 14.365,
  unchanged.

## E48 batch 5: every drawing Stained Glass wears on the 24 grid (21f9dd2c; not yet seen by the owner)

- Under Stained Glass, Foundry's scene-controls rail, sidebar tabs and window-header buttons wear the 24 set: 60
  chrome masks drawn on the 24 grid, each in a box of max(1.15em, 22px) like the rest of the glass set (read in the
  mock and the glass harness, not in a real Foundry). The six small markers (diamond, diamond-empty, dot, dot-empty,
  skull, query) are drawn on 24 as well. Monokuma Legacy is unchanged: the diff leaves its rules byte for byte, and R3596 holds Legacy's 12 drawing on each chrome selector. The owner's Q11
  rule is met as R3339 reads it: R3339 is green and its `expectedRed("E48")` marker is off. Whether the drawings
  please the owner is not known: they were published for the owner's look on 12.11.2026 (Known gaps).
- Four rows are named for their meaning (clear-all, daylight, darkness, ethereal-wall), because trash, sun, moon
  and mask are drawings the glass already wears on the module's own markup; circle-regular and folder wear
  glass:circle and glass:file-pick through a row marked `same`, as chrome:circle-regular already shares chrome:circle;
  that Foundry's folder button and the module's file pick are one function is not shown (Known gaps).
- Red at 17aceda8's glyphs.json with this commit's tests: "1 passed, 2 failed" (R3339 66 off the grid; R3596 66
  problems); green, with every tier 0-1 test that reads the glyph files, "32 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped" (R515,
  skipped by its own check of what the harness can read). The quick check green on its tree: lint, the checks and the
  gate's self-test, the Polish file, its own two tests, scenarios 71 and 75 and the glass harness. The drawings, their
  sheets and shots are the stage's working files, not in the repository.
